title: Measurement: Length, Weight & Capacity
description: Class 2 IMO — Measurement: comparing and measuring length, weight and capacity with standard units (cm, m, kg, litre) and everyday-maths problems.

topics.title: Length (cm and m)
topics.concept: Length is how long something is. We measure short lengths in centimetres (cm) and longer ones in metres (m). 1 m = 100 cm. A pencil is about 15 cm; a door is about 2 m. We still compare with longer and shorter.

examples.problem: Which unit suits the length of a classroom — cm or m?
examples.solution: Metres (m), because a classroom is long.

examples.problem: A ribbon is 30 cm and another is 45 cm. Which is longer?

recap: Short lengths: centimetres (cm). Long lengths: metres (m).

quiz.q: Which is best measured in metres?
quiz.explanation: A cricket pitch is long, so metres.

topics.title: Weight (kg)
topics.concept: Weight tells how heavy something is. We measure it in kilograms (kg). A bag of rice may be 5 kg; an apple is much less than 1 kg. We compare with heavier and lighter and use a balance to weigh.

examples.problem: Which is heavier — 2 kg of sugar or 5 kg of sugar?
A watermelon is about 3 kg. Is an apple more or less than that?

recap: Compare with heavier / lighter; use a balance.

quiz.explanation: A packet of sugar is about 1 kg.

topics.title: Capacity (litre)
topics.concept: Capacity is how much a container can hold. We measure liquids in litres (L). A water bottle may hold 1 litre; a bucket holds many litres; a spoon holds much less than a litre.

examples.problem: A bucket holds 8 L and is filled with two 4 L jugs. Does that fill it?

recap: Buckets hold many litres; spoons hold very little.

quiz.explanation: Milk is a liquid, measured in litres.

quiz.q: A jug holds 2 L. How much do 3 such jugs hold?

questions.q: Odd one out (three measure length, one does not):  cm, m, kg, metre?
questions.explanation: kg measures weight; the others measure length.

questions.q: Litre is to capacity as kilogram is to ___ ?
Order from shortest to longest: 5 cm, 50 cm, 5 m. Which is longest?
Which unit measures the length of your notebook?
questions.explanation: A notebook's length is in centimetres.

questions.q: 1 m = 100 cm. How many cm is 2 m?
A rope is 9 m long. 3 m is cut off. How much is left?
A bag of potatoes weighs 8 kg and a bag of onions 5 kg. How much heavier are the potatoes?
Amma needs 10 L of water and has filled 6 L. How much more is needed?
A cloth piece is 3 m long. Each dress needs 1 m. How many dresses can be made?
A bucket holds 12 L. It is filled using a 3 L mug. How many mugs of water fill it?
Two ribbons are 35 cm and 45 cm. Joined together, what is the total length?
